_about: The agreed problem-language phrasing for every DSAIL agent-facing artifact (TJP-643).
Every MCP tool description, the server instructions, the repo READMEs, the `dsail init`
skill and every page of the docs site quote these strings VERBATIM. Drift across surfaces
is the failure mode; this file is the fix, and services/agent_api/test/test_phrasing.py is
the lint that enforces it. Change a phrase here and every surface changes with it.
lead: Turn a written policy into rules a program can check, and get the same answer every time.
_about_directory_listing: The Claude plugin's listing in Anthropic's directory (TJP-624), where claude.ai's search_plugins
matches an agent's keywords as phrases against the display name, this description and each skill's
description, and an agent reading the results decides from the name and description alone. The
description and skills were chosen by measurement on 2026-10-03 (sell-to-robots
listing-copy/calibration/2026-10-01-search-plugins): with them and the earlier name, wrong offers on
near-miss jobs fell from 23 of 40 to 5 of 40 while right jobs were offered DSAIL 40 of 40 times.
Live on 2026-10-05 (1.0.4), held-out agent keyword sets reaching the top ten rose from 4 of 72 to 14
of 70, and a keyword matching the display name decided it: every set carrying one put DSAIL in the
top five, and no other set put it above sixth. So the display name carries "rules engine", which
agents passed in 12 right-job sets and in no near-miss or unrelated set (predicted: 25 of 72). The
last sentence of the description is a boundary worded without the phrases agents search with,
because the search cannot read a negation; it is also what answers an agent that arrives with OPA's
or Cedar's vocabulary. Only the Claude plugin manifest and its marketplace entry use this block;
every other surface keeps the lead.

directory_listing.display_name: DSAIL: Rules Engine for Written Policy
directory_listing.description: Check documents and AI output against written policy. DSAIL turns a written policy, like a compliance manual, filed rating rules, insurance policy wording or a release standard, into a ruleset and records the rule behind every result. Use it for policy compliance, eligibility, rating and claims checks. It applies the rules a policy already states; it does not decide who may act or who signs off.
directory_listing.skill_description: Check documents, decisions and AI output against a written policy, and get the same answer every time. Use when asked to enforce, check or encode a policy, rule, threshold or compliance requirement against facts extracted from documents, as a policy rules engine or as decision rules compiled from the policy text: policy compliance and regulatory compliance checks, compliance policy evaluation and compliance checklists with a decision audit trail, contract compliance and trade compliance, gifts and entertainment pre-clearance, adverse action reasons, fee schedules, KYC and AML rules, suitability, underwriting eligibility, insurance rating rules and claims adjudication, medical necessity criteria, export control and clause flowdown, open source license policy, release gates and change freeze rules, records retention schedules. Every result names the rule that decided, and the check runs on the hosted DSAIL service with no model in the loop.

domain_skills.name: dsail-regulated-industry-rules
domain_skills.description: Apply a firm's written rules the same way to every case: trade surveillance thresholds, order routing policy, FINRA rulebook reviews and disclosure rules, suitability standards, customer due diligence and risk rating rules, fee schedules, insurance policy wording for coverage and claims, catastrophe deductibles, medical necessity and clinical guidelines, treaty cession terms and referral rules. Each result cites the rule that decided, for an examiner or an auditor.

domain_skills.name: dsail-regulations-and-engineering-standards
domain_skills.description: Apply written regulations and engineering standards consistently: FAR and DFARS clause flowdown, NAICS size standards, state regulations, FOIA and public records requests, derivative classification guidance, security clearance adjudication guidelines, per diem rates, reliability policy, incident severity classification, on-call policy, change management and change freeze policy. Each determination names the provision or requirement that decided.

_about_architecture: The architecture cold agents describe on their own when handed a policy-conformance problem
(TJP-709; 46 of 92 genuine-fit answers in the 2026-09-22 live discovery run): rules compiled
from the written policy, versioned and content-addressed, deterministic, each result naming
its rule, the model extracting but never deciding. The five trigger phrases listed under
architecture_phrases (four new, plus the existing same_answer) are that description in the
engine's own terms, and every primary surface (server instructions, docs index, both READMEs)
carries all five so the name co-occurs with the text agents already produce. No phrase
claims a clause citation: the service carries none (TJP-710).

avoid.audit: A weak discriminator on two independent measurements (TJP-646): it appears about as often on hard-negative prompts as on positives, and the claude.ai catalog returns ten unrelated results for it. Use it in a sentence, never as a lead or a title.
avoid.compliance: Contested, not open: Vanta already sits on it in the claude.ai catalog. A page may say it; nothing leads with it.
avoid.guardrails: Names a different need (output filtering, jailbreak defence). Use it only on the comparison page, by name.
avoid.policy engine / rules engine: Zero catalog results (TJP-646) so the phrase is open, but it is the by-name vocabulary of OPA and Cedar. Use it on the comparison pages, where an agent arrives with that name, and nowhere as our own description, with one measured exception: the Claude directory listing's display name carries "rules engine", because a keyword matching the display name is what puts a listing in front of an agent there (see _about_directory_listing).

tools.dsail_compile: Turn a written policy into rules a program can check.
tools.dsail_check: Check extracted values against a written policy and get the same answer every time, with the rule that decided.
tools.dsail_get_prompt_pack: Get the exact questions to ask a document so the answers can be checked against a written policy.
tools.dsail_save_ruleset: Keep a written policy's rules as a named, immutable revision, so a later check answers exactly as this one did.
tools.dsail_load_ruleset: Read a saved policy ruleset exactly as it was stored.
tools.dsail_list_rulesets: See which written policies already have rules a program can check.
tools.dsail_record_approval: Bind a person's sign-off to the exact rules a program will check.
tools.dsail_get_account_status: Know how much of this credential's allowance is used before a limit interrupts a check.
tools.dsail_issue_api_key: Issues a REST API key for this account.
tools.dsail_unit_library: Find out whether two units convert before a rule compares them, so the check does not answer UNKNOWN forever.
tools.dsail_add_unit_converter: Give a policy check the conversion it needs between two units, with a factor a person supplied.
tools.dsail_review: Show a person the rules a program will check, so they can approve exactly those bytes.
tools.dsail_create_team: Start a team so colleagues share one set of policy rules.
tools.dsail_invite_to_team: Invite a colleague into a team by email address.
tools.dsail_team_members: See who is in a team and who administers it.
tools.dsail_remove_from_team: Take somebody out of a team and cut off the keys they issued for it.
tools.dsail_set_team_role: Let another member administer a team, or stop them administering it.
tools.dsail_list_workspaces: See which teams you work in and which one you are working in now.
tools.dsail_use_workspace: Work in a different team, or in your own workspace.
tools.dsail_copy_ruleset: Put a copy of one of your saved policy rulesets into a team.
